decisions.reason: Preserving consistency and frothiness during dispensing does not necessarily change the existing open/close valve or tap actuation mechanism.
The source adds a beverage-preservation constraint but does not change the requirement to prevent leakage into the base.
Revising the spout to preserve beverage texture does not necessarily alter its required barista-facing orientation.
The candidate already records the same message's diagram-matching appearance requirement; the separate texture-preservation clause does not change that visual requirement.
The source concerns preserving already mixed matcha while it passes through the spout, not changing the required mixing output or foam production.
The beverage-preservation constraint does not modify the independent requirement preventing liquid from reaching electronics.
The source does not change the enclosure thickness or overall size constraints.
Retaining consistency and frothiness through the spout does not necessarily alter the independent splash-minimization requirement.
The source addresses downstream dispensing effects and does not change the whisk dimensions, powder compatibility, or bowl-capacity basis.
The dispensing-preservation change does not modify bowl depth, 4.5-quart capacity, or the acceptability of refilling.
The spout and beverage-preservation decision has no necessary effect on the wiring-plan deliverable.
The source does not change the independent requirement that the spout be removable or easy to flush and clean.
